⛔ ROLE → TIER, SO A PERSON IS NOT LEVEL 1 FOR WANT OF ONE FIELD. Aevi, ASK_generate_the_forty: 'NOT A MISSING SHEET. NOT A MISSING KIT. ONE MISSING FIELD.' All 40 level-1 records were level 1 for exactly one reason — no `tier` — while `tierFloor` (riffraff 1 · notable 5 · regional 12 · heroic 25 · epic 40 · legendary 60 · mythic 85) already fires for the 64 who have one. ⚠️ THE ROLE STRING ALREADY SAYS WHICH RUNG: 'a toll-collector is not a heroic and a self-appointed keeper of the Lost Archive is not riffraff.' Same shape as the 43 tag→family mappings — the prose already clusters and nobody had read it.
⛑ THIS TABLE IS CONTENT, DELIBERATELY. The engine derives; the JUDGEMENT about which rung a role sits on is Aevi's and Erik's, and every row here can be corrected without touching code. A record's own authored `tier` ALWAYS wins over anything here.
_howItIsRead: ⛔ FIRST MATCH WINS, IN ORDER, and the order is the whole design: DEMOTING patterns are listed FIRST so 'young keeper' reads as notable rather than regional. `match` is a case-insensitive regular expression tested against the record's `role` string. A record matching nothing takes `default`.
_theGuardThatMatters: ⛔ DEFAULT DOWN, NEVER UP (Aevi): 'a wrong guess that makes someone weaker is a disappointment; one that makes them stronger is an ambush.' MEASURED: at level 1 a person has 35 health and 1 craft; at heroic they have 155 health and 13. Guessing one rung high is a foe with a hundred more health, so nothing here promotes past `heroic` — epic, legendary and mythic are AUTHORED RUNGS ONLY. A figure whose story earns one of those gets it from a person, not from a regex.
_ceilingWhy: ⛔ THE HIGHEST A DERIVATION MAY REACH. Above this the rung is a claim about the world's great figures — `_theMythicalRung` calls them hinges — and a pattern match is not entitled to make it.

rules.why: ⚠️ DEMOTES FIRST, AND ON PURPOSE. `young_ent_lissome` is 'a young Ent who wants to walk out into the wider world'; `burr_the_foundling` is 'a human child half-adopted by the Glade'. Youth outranks every promoting word that follows it — a young keeper is not a keeper yet.

⚑ AGE AND PRECEDENCE AS STANDING. `rootbound_vaskar` is an 'Ancient Ent hardliner'; `reed_mother_ossa` is the 'aging matriarch and moral center of the Greywater Stilts'; `high_luminary` is 'Master of the Radiant Plateau'.
⚑ A TITLE THAT COMMANDS. `elder_resonance` is 'Master of the Harmonic Heights'; `champion_vael` is a 'Marcher champion'; `marshal_veyn` 'has held a line and she has lost one'.

⚑ AN ELDER SPEAKS FOR A PEOPLE. `walker_elder_thren` argues to keep the Deepwood woven into the world; `wend_elder_saba` is a dying Wend elder. ⚠️ Listed after the youth demotion so 'young elder' cannot promote.

⚑ RESPONSIBILITY FOR A PLACE OR A THING. `warden_isolde` keeps the Green Accord; `keeper_ilma` has kept the accountability board thirty years; `archive_guardian` is the self-appointed keeper of the Lost Archive.

⚑ AUTHORITY OVER A PROCESS. `broker_sain` holds neutrality at the Center; `mediator_corran` holds a border town's balance; `fendt` is a filtration supervisor. ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-12 ADDED THE COUNCIL SEAT: "Dara Holt is the ditchmother and on the Millbrook Council, she should be leveled too." A seat on the body that decides a place's business is authority over a process, which is this row's own sentence — so it is his judgement recorded here rather than a new rule competing with it. ⚠️ AEVI: widen or re-word freely; `ditch-mother` and the other honorifics are deliberately NOT here, because a title is a claim about one person and this table is about roles.

⚑ A PRACTISED CRAFT, DEEP ENOUGH TO BE THEIR NAME. `archivist_lom` is 'a Cogitant of the Cogitarium'; `solvace` is a 'Blazeborn lens-wright'; `the_ferryman_tam` is a channel-pilot who knows every secret in the marsh.

⚠️ A TRADE THAT TRAVELS OR FETCHES — real competence, no standing. `brann_tollhand` is a 'toll-collector at the Roost's lower gate; small crook with a soft spot'; `mountain_scout` is a 'young explorer who found the new pass'; `sable_the_runner` is a pass-runner.

_whatIsNotHere: ⚠️ NO `communityId` OR `assistTags` RULES YET, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Aevi named all three as inputs; ROLE alone resolves all 40 defensibly, and a second signal that agrees with the first adds nothing while a second that disagrees needs a precedence rule nobody has ruled on. ⛑ If a role proves unreadable for a future record, an `assistTags` tie-breaker is the next thing to author — the engine already passes the whole record to the deriver.
_whatThisCannotDo_20260908: ⛔ THIS TABLE CANNOT MINT ANYTHING ABOVE `heroic`, BY DESIGN — and that is a rule about AUTHORING, not a limitation to work around. ⚑ CCode: 'a derivation must never mint a legendary — epic, legendary and mythic are a claim about the world's great figures, and a REGEX IS NOT ENTITLED TO MAKE IT.' ⚠️ SO: ANY BEING ABOVE HEROIC MUST CARRY AN AUTHORED `tier`. A legendary, an epic, a mythic, a Sovereign, a dragon — if the record does not say, the derivation will read the role string and give them the honest small answer. ⛑ THE LIVE EXAMPLE, AND IT IS A DRAGON: `tolvess` is role 'A YOUNG true dragon' — ⛔ and `young` matches the FIRST rule, which demotes. ⚠️ Without his authored `tier: epic` he would be NOTABLE at level 5: a three-hundred-year-old dragon fought as a villager. ⚑ Nothing is wrong today because authored always wins — but the trap is one omitted field deep. ⬜ AND NO DRAGON ROW WAS ADDED ON PURPOSE. Naming 'dragon' or 'wyrm' here would let a regex mint a legendary, which is the one thing the ceiling forbids. ⛔ THE FIX IS ON THE AUTHOR'S SIDE: write the tier.
_ceilingRemoved_20260908: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-08 OVERRULES THE CEILING: 'ELIMINATE THE NO-GENERATED-NPCS-PAST-THIS-TIER RULE. That's not what I want. WE CAN MAKE IT RARE, BUT THE GAME IS PRIMARILY GENERATIVE.' ⚠️ CCode's reasoning was 'a derivation must never mint a legendary — epic, legendary and mythic are a claim about the world's great figures, and a regex is not entitled to make it', and AEVI ENDORSED IT TWICE. ⛑ The concern is real; the CEILING was the wrong answer to it. ⛔ AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLES IT: the authored population is an INVERTED PYRAMID — heroic 41, epic 35, legendary 29, and ZERO riffraff, notable or regional. ⚠️ A ceiling was defending a shape the corpus does not have, while the ACTUAL scarcity problem is that nobody has authored the bottom. ⚑ WHAT REPLACES IT IS RARITY, NOT PROHIBITION — see `_rarityReplacesCeiling`. ⬜ `_whatThisCannotDo_20260908` is SUPERSEDED in its conclusion and kept for its example: `tolvess` reading 'A YOUNG true dragon' still trips the demoting rule, and an authored tier still wins. ⛔ THAT PART WAS ALWAYS TRUE AND IS NOT ABOUT THE CEILING.
_rarityReplacesCeiling_20260908: ⬜ SPEC FOR CCODE — `SPEC_generation_reaches_every_tier.md`. ⚑ THREE GUARDS INSTEAD OF ONE WALL: (1) RARITY BY POPULATION SHAPE, not by rule. A generated tier is drawn against the world's EXISTING census — if legendaries are already 12% of the population, another is vanishingly unlikely; if the bottom is empty, riffraff is nearly certain. ⚠️ THE PYRAMID ENFORCES ITSELF AND SELF-CORRECTS. (2) EVIDENCE PROPORTIONAL TO CLAIM. A role string alone reaches heroic — that much of CCode's instinct holds. ⛔ ABOVE IT NEEDS MORE: arc involvement, an authored renown, a `hingeNpcs` mention, a region's own tier band, or deeds already recorded in `figureCareer`. ⚑ A regex is not entitled to mint a legendary; A BODY OF EVIDENCE IS. (3) VISIBLE AND CORRECTABLE. `tierDerived` rides on the sheet and the roster marks every guess with `~`, so a minted legendary is one edit from being demoted by a human who disagrees. ⛔ AND THE DEFAULT STILL FALLS DOWN, not up: an unreadable role is `notable`. ⚠️ Erik: 'we can make it RARE' — rare is a rate, and a rate is not zero.
